Reason and Result Clauses Using Participles
As an alternative to using linking words with conjunctions, you can use participles to introduce a reason or a result of something. A participle is a verb + ing.
For example:
To express result instead of words like because and as a result.

Having finished the assignment, I asked my boss to read it over.
Considering that this book is going to become a monster, she'd better get used to it.
To express reason instead of words like so and therefore.

Being a little tired, I think I may head home myself.
Seeing that she had a very big day, I would imagine she is tired.
Being a little tired, I think I may head home myself.
Having finished our speeches and introductions and considering that it's getting a little late in the evening, I suggest you now work the room.
Seeing that she had a very big day, I would imagine she is tired.
Having said that, I'm going to have a drink.
Considering that this book is going to become a monster, she'd better get used to it.
The Present Continuous and Be Going To
You use the Present Continuous tense to talk about a variety of situations. You use be going to to talk about the future.

Denise: Well gang, having finished our speeches and introductions and considering that it's getting a little late in the evening, I suggest you now work the room. Do one more sweep first, then I would like you to mingle and give out your business cards. Don't go overboard and drink too much and don't overstep your bounds with anyone, but have some fun. Having said that, I'm going to have a drink.
Adam: Oh no! I only have a couple of business cards left.
Boris: You are always doing that. Here, take some of mine. Let's mingle.
Kristi: Denise. Where is Marisa?
Denise: I think she is off having a heart attack somewhere. Poor thing. No, Marisa's leaving for the station in about a minute.
Kristi: Is she going somewhere else?
Denise: I think she is going home. She is going on some kind of excursion tomorrow. Seeing that she's had a very big day, I would imagine she is tired.

Kristi: Considering that this book is going to become a monster, she'd better get used to it.
Denise: Being a little tired, I think I may head home myself.

Adam walks over to a colleague having a conversation with a lovely young lady. The lady looks very bored.

Ben: So, this guy is sitting all by himself in a bar moping, so the barman refuses to serve him another drink.
Adam: Denise needs to see you right away. It's important.
Ben: Oh, excuse me!
Adam: He usually prefers tea to liquor.
Martina: Are you going to finish telling the rest of that horrible joke?
Adam: I don't know any horrible jokes.

Martina: You're funny.
Adam: Thanks, my mom concurs as well.
Martina: Sadly, I have to be going. I am tasked with going to a very boring family event now and I'm running late, but here's my card.
Adam: Oh excellent. Here's mine.
Martina: Thanks, see you around funny man.
Adam: See you around.

Boris comes up behind Adam

Boris: Who was that? She was stunning.
Adam: That was ... Martina.
Boris: Are you going to call her?
Adam: Oh yeah. Oh wait! Oh no. I think I gave her one of your business cards by mistake. I'm so stupid!
Boris: Nice work. Funny man.
